tolerance_note: A difference is |TA-Lib - other| divided by a scale: 1 for outputs in points (the 0 to 100 readings), the largest absolute TA-Lib value for volume outputs, and for every other output its own typical size (the median absolute TA-Lib value of that output; see tests/indicator_scale.py). The scale is not the price: the MACD histogram and the ATR are small next to it. An entry listed below under a library is compared by the stated mode; every other entry must match within default_tolerance wherever both libraries have a value.

pandas_ta_classic.role: Second library of record. It has its own pandas implementation of every menu entry (called with talib=False) and agrees with TA-Lib to rounding error on all but two entries. Its code deliberately follows TA-Lib's conventions in many places, so agreement shows correct inputs, parameters and outputs rather than an independent opinion on conventions; talipp supplies that.

CCI.reason: Rounding error only. CCI is unbounded and often in the hundreds, and it divides by a mean deviation, so the absolute rounding error is larger than for other point-valued entries (observed worst 5e-11).

MACD.reason: pandas-ta-classic runs the fast average as an ordinary EMA from the first candle. TA-Lib starts the fast average late, at the first candle where the slow average exists, from the mean of the fast-length candles ending there (reproduced in test_talib_macd_fast_average_is_seeded_where_the_slow_average_starts using only TA-Lib's own EMA). The lines differ at the start and converge as the earlier seed fades.
MACD.tradingview: Unverified recollection of the Pine Script reference (not checked in this task, not covered by T27 acceptance): ta.macd is recalled as subtracting two ordinary EMAs; how those EMAs are seeded is not known, so whether its early values match this library, TA-Lib or neither is not known.

SAR.reason: Parabolic SAR remembers its trend, extreme point and acceleration, so one early difference can persist until the next reversal. pandas-ta-classic makes its first step after the start with zero acceleration, where TA-Lib uses the initial acceleration (bars 2-10 of trend_pullback). TA-Lib also reverses when a low exactly touches the SAR, while pandas-ta-classic needs the low to go below it: in range_burst the low equals the SAR at bar 407, TA-Lib reverses there and pandas-ta-classic two bars later, and the two paths differ until bar 420.
SAR.tradingview: Unverified recollection of the Pine Script reference (not checked in this task, not covered by T27 acceptance): ta.sar has its own start rules, not known here; treat the first candles of any history, and the candles right after a reversal, as library-specific.

talipp.role: Convention probe. A pure-Python library with no dependencies and no TA-Lib code or reference to it. It has no Money Flow Index and no momentum, so those two entries are compared against pandas-ta-classic only. Its seeding conventions differ from TA-Lib's in the Wilder-smoothed indicators, which makes it the evidence for the documented differences.

CCI.reason: Rounding error only. CCI is unbounded and often in the hundreds, and it divides by a mean deviation, so the absolute rounding error is larger than for other point-valued entries (observed worst 7e-10).

MFI.reason: talipp has no Money Flow Index.

MOM.reason: talipp has rate of change but no price-difference momentum.

STOCH.reason: talipp's Stoch returns the raw %K and a simple average of it as %D. That equals TA-Lib's slow stochastic only when the slow-K smoothing is 1, so it is compared only for those settings.

MACD.reason: Same cause as for pandas-ta-classic: talipp runs the fast average as an ordinary EMA from the first candle, TA-Lib seeds it where the slow average begins.
MACD.tradingview: Unverified recollection of the Pine Script reference (not checked in this task, not covered by T27 acceptance): ta.macd is recalled as subtracting two ordinary EMAs; how those EMAs are seeded is not known, so whether its early values match this library, TA-Lib or neither is not known.

SAR.reason: talipp needs four candles before its first SAR and starts from a different initial trend and extreme point than TA-Lib. The paths realign at a later reversal (bar 38 of trend_pullback, bar 420 of range_burst).
SAR.tradingview: Unverified recollection of the Pine Script reference (not checked in this task, not covered by T27 acceptance): ta.sar has its own start rules, not known here; treat the first candles of any history, and the candles right after a reversal, as library-specific.

ADX.reason: talipp divides its smoothed directional movement by an ATR that counts the first candle's high minus low as a true range and seeds with plain averages of the first N values. TA-Lib seeds the smoothed sums with the first N-1 values and applies the first smoothing step at candle N (found by fitting hand-derived values; TA-Lib documents no formula). Wilder smoothing forgets its seed by a factor (N-1)/N per candle, and ADX smooths twice, so the gap takes about 21 periods to fall below one hundred-millionth of the output (measured).
ADX.tradingview: Unverified recollection of the Pine Script reference (not checked in this task, not covered by T27 acceptance): ta.dmi is recalled as using ta.rma, which starts from a simple average of the first N values, with a first true range of high minus low, which would behave like talipp here.

PLUS_DI.reason: Same seeding difference as ADX; the directional indicators are one smoothing deep, so they settle slightly sooner.

MINUS_DI.reason: Same seeding difference as ADX; the directional indicators are one smoothing deep, so they settle slightly sooner.

ATR.reason: talipp counts the first candle's high minus low as a true range and averages candles 0 to N-1 for its first value. TA-Lib's true range needs a previous close, so it starts at the second candle and averages candles 1 to N. After the seed both smooth by Wilder's rule, so the gap shrinks by (N-1)/N per candle.
ATR.tradingview: Unverified recollection of the Pine Script reference (not checked in this task, not covered by T27 acceptance): ta.atr is recalled as smoothing ta.tr with ta.rma, with ta.tr equal to high minus low on the first candle, which would behave like talipp here.

NATR.reason: Normalised ATR is the ATR above divided by the close, so it carries the same seed difference. It is measured in percent against its own size, which is under one percent of the close, so it needs as many periods as the ATR.
